rails.principle: A visual redesign preserves product intent.
rails.recommendation: Preserve the core task, useful existing behavior, and accurate content unless a human decision changes them.
rails.context: A visual improvement should not silently change what the product says or does.
rails.escapeCondition: Change behavior or content when an explicit human decision supports the product goal; record the decision and any required content review.

rails.recommendation: Use the existing platform and stack by default; explain a new dependency when it materially helps.
rails.context: This keeps changes aligned with the project and avoids incidental complexity.
rails.escapeCondition: Introduce a dependency when a concrete requirement is difficult to meet with existing tools and the project accepts its maintenance cost.

rails.principle: Treat content and user data as product responsibilities.
rails.recommendation: Do not invent product facts or endorsements, expose private data, or add a network request without a project need.
rails.context: A polished interface must remain accurate and respect the project's privacy boundaries.
rails.escapeCondition: Use real claims or data only when an authoritative project source and the applicable review process support them; add network behavior only for an approved product requirement.

rails.principle: Use material the project has permission to use.
rails.recommendation: Attribute references and do not copy unlicensed assets, wording, or a complete visual identity.
rails.context: A reference can inform a named quality without granting rights to its material.
rails.escapeCondition: Reuse an asset or text only when the project has verified permission and records any required attribution.
